clue.text: Delete at the end of industrial action

definitions.meaning: to remove a name from a list or register

definitions.text: at the end of industrial action
definitions.meaning: when a stoppage of work is called off, the walkout is over

explanation.surface: A union leader announces something is to be deleted once the walkout finishes.
explanation.definitionFit: To remove from a register is a synonym; read as a phrase, the stoppage is called off, which marks the close of the dispute.

clue.text: One with a lot to say when hunter loses his head

definitions.text: One with a lot to say

indicators.note: loses his head means the hunter word drops its first letter

parts.note: a stalker is a hunter who tracks prey

explanation.surface: A chatterbox appears when a hunter is decapitated.
explanation.definitionFit: A chatterbox or speaker is someone who has plenty to say.

clue.text: Entirely enthusiastic about the said duo

parts.note: to be into something is to be keen on it

indicators.note: said signals a word heard rather than seen, so duo's synonym is replaced by its homophone

parts.note: a duo is two

explanation.surface: Someone is wholly keen on a famous double act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the' is a link; TWO, said aloud, gives TO.
explanation.definitionFit: A Latin phrase meaning as a whole, completely.

clue.text: Old call to arouse feelings

parts.note: ex means former or old
to cite is to call or summon, as to court

explanation.surface: A former partner's phone call stirs up emotions.
explanation.definitionFit: To stir up or stimulate emotions is a synonym.

clue.text: Does the winner's reward come from the orchard?

definitions.text: Does the winner's reward come from the orchard?

parts.words: Does the winner's reward come from the orchard?
parts.note: the spoils of a triumph read as produce picked from trees

explanation.definitionFit: The benefits gained by winning are called by a phrase that also suggests apples and pears.

clue.text: Next to a tall team

parts.note: long means tall
a side is a team

explanation.surface: Standing beside a very tall team.
explanation.definitionFit: Beside and adjacent are synonyms for being close by.

clue.text: Became more precipitous or more pricey?…

definitions.meaning: grew sharper in incline
steep also means expensive, so this reads as made dearer

explanation.surface: A slope got sharper, or perhaps prices went up.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is an incline growing sharper; the other plays on steep meaning overpriced.

clue.text: … precipitousness of a cliff in Kent

definitions.meaning: the vertical steepness of a rock face
a port town in the English county of Kent

explanation.surface: The steepness of a clifftop in Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: SHEERNESS is a port town on the Isle of Sheppey in Kent, a county in south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheer means vertical, so the noun is steepness; it is also a Kentish town on the Thames estuary.

clue.text: Part of the car to hold on to

definitions.meaning: the pedal or mechanism that engages the gears
to grip tightly

explanation.surface: A driving instructor names a part of the car you must keep a grip on.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the gear-engaging pedal of a vehicle; the other is a verb meaning grasp tightly.

clue.text: Society overdue with 100 in advance payment

indicators.note: the word in places the overdue part and the number inside the payment

parts.note: a sub is a payment made in advance of wages
overdue means late
the setter means CL, Roman 150; Roman 100 alone is C

explanation.surface: A society chases a member whose advance payment, along with a sum, is overdue.
explanation.walkthrough: A SLATE CLUB is a British savings club whose members pay in weekly. The clue prints 100, which gives only C; the letters need CL, Roman 150, so the number is a slip.
explanation.definitionFit: A savings club is a kind of mutual society, so the club stands as an example of the defining word.

clue.text: Remain firm in this place

definitions.meaning: to be fixed or inherent in something
inside here, at this spot

explanation.surface: An instruction to stay firm and not leave this spot.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a verb meaning to be intrinsic or permanently fixed; the other splits into two words meaning inside this spot.

clue.text: Impoverished Desmond takes it back to you in Nice before half-term

parts.note: Des is the short form of the name Desmond

indicators.note: back means the word it is turned round to read the other way

parts.note: tu is the familiar French for you, as spoken in Nice

indicators.note: half signals that only the first two letters of the word term are used

explanation.surface: A man named Desmond carries something back to you in a French resort before half-term.
explanation.walkthrough: Nice is the French city, so 'you in Nice' asks for the French familiar pronoun; 'takes', 'to' and 'before' are links, and 'back' turns the word it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Destitute and impoverished are synonyms describing someone lacking money and the basics of life.

clue.text: A rigid back

parts.note: stern means strict or rigid

explanation.surface: Something described as stiff and unbending in the spine.
explanation.definitionFit: On a ship, towards the rear is a nautical synonym for going backwards.

clue.text: Guy that will only frighten one bird?

parts.note: to scare is to frighten
a crow is one kind of bird

explanation.surface: A dummy figure that merely frightens off a single bird.
explanation.walkthrough: A guy is a stuffed effigy burnt on British bonfire night; 'that will only' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are stuffed straw figures dressed in old clothes, an effigy.

clue.text: Unique like an empty box of firelighters

definitions.meaning: without equal

definitions.text: like an empty box of firelighters
definitions.meaning: lacking any of the small sticks you strike to make fire

explanation.surface: A one-off item compared to a used-up box of fire starters.
explanation.definitionFit: Without equal is a synonym; read literally, it describes a box with none of its sticks left.

clue.text: Concert contract

definitions.meaning: concert can mean harmony or accord, as in acting in concert
a binding deal

explanation.surface: A music event's contract.
explanation.definitionFit: Accord or harmony is a sense of concert; a binding deal is another word for a contract.

clue.text: Man shortly will move quickly up and down

definitions.meaning: a shortened form of the man's name Robert
to bounce or jerk up and down, as a cork on water

explanation.surface: A fellow, briefly, who will soon be jumping up and down.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a nickname for Robert; the other is a verb for bouncing, as a float does on water.

clue.text: Snake is in the gazebo ante-room

indicators.note: in signals that the answer sits inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A serpent lurks in the garden pavilion's entry room.
explanation.definitionFit: The constrictor of South America is a kind of snake.

clue.text: One taken in by graduate might sound sheepish

indicators.note: taken in by means one letter is placed inside the graduate's letters

parts.note: BA is a Bachelor of Arts, a graduate
a means one

explanation.surface: Someone fooled by a graduate might look embarrassed.
explanation.definitionFit: The bleat of a sheep, so a pun on sounding like a sheep.

clue.text: Moving speech?

parts.note: read not as an emotional oration but as the words you use when telling people you have relocated home

explanation.definitionFit: When you relocate, you notify people of your new home details, a form of notice tied to moving house.

clue.text: Drivers' club against including this lady

indicators.note: including means the drivers' club letters wrap round the letter for against

parts.note: the AA is the Automobile Association, a British motoring organisation
v is short for versus, against

explanation.surface: A motoring organisation takes a stand against admitting a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Ava is a woman's first name, so a female name stands for the pronoun phrase.

clue.text: Bat noise?

definitions.meaning: a strung bat used in tennis or squash
a din or loud row

explanation.surface: A question whether a flying mammal makes a sound.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the strung bat of tennis; the other is a loud din.

clue.text: Shrub I removed with arrogance

indicators.note: removed, read as re-moved, says the letters are moved around again

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bush is cleared away with a haughty attitude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removed' looks like deletion but means moved again; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessive pride, arrogance in Greek tragedy, is the meaning.

clue.text: Endlessly grip (twice) an African charm

indicators.note: twice says the shortened piece is written two times
endlessly means the word grip loses its last letter

explanation.surface: Holding tight on repeat to a talisman from Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: An amulet or talisman worn in parts of Africa against evil.

clue.text: Piece of chant's arranged

indicators.note: arranged says the letters of the word chant's are set out anew

explanation.surface: A section of a chant is arranged for performance.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's counts as a letter here, giving CHANTS to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A fragment or short bit, as a snatch of song.

clue.text: Happening to be found by the arena

parts.note: to occur can mean to exist or be found somewhere
a ring is an arena, as for boxing or a circus

explanation.surface: An event taking place, discovered beside the stadium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' just places one piece next to the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking place and happening are synonyms for an event under way.

clue.text: Supporter of journalism

definitions.meaning: a pillar that holds up a roof or structure
a regular article or feature in a newspaper

explanation.definitionFit: A pillar holds up a building, and a regular newspaper feature shares the name.

clue.text: Urge actor somehow to produce ridged effect

indicators.note: somehow says the letters are put together in some new way

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A director urges an actor to create a ridged effect somehow.
explanation.definitionFit: To corrugate is to fold metal or card into parallel ridges and grooves.

clue.text: Some errors in overacting a Shakespearean part

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A critic notes a few mistakes in an over-the-top performance of a Shakespeare role.
explanation.definitionFit: Orsino is the Duke of Illyria in Twelfth Night, a role in a play by the Bard.

clue.text: Salute to Conservatism?

definitions.meaning: a parade-ground command to turn the head in salute
looking towards the political right wing

explanation.surface: A gesture of respect offered to the Conservative cause.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a military order to turn the head in salute; literally it means looking towards the political right.
